en.headline: Diagonal pedestrian crossing opens near Shek Mun Station in Sha Tin
en.dek: The Transport Department commissioned the junction of On Ming and On Muk streets on Tuesday, the latest of 15 planned sites expected to cut walking distance by about 30 per cent.
body: A diagonal pedestrian crossing at the junction of On Ming Street and On Muk Street in Sha Tin was commissioned on Tuesday, the Transport Department said, allowing people to cross the intersection in one movement.

The crossing is near MTR Shek Mun Station and Shek Mun Shopping Centre. Dropped kerbs have been added for the elderly, wheelchair users and people with handcarts, and traffic bollards have been installed to remind motorists to drive carefully.

The department said overall operations of two earlier trial crossings in Sha Tin and Tsim Sha Tsui had been safe and smooth since 2024. Walking distance and time are expected to be reduced by about 30 per cent on average compared with right-angle crossings. Diagonal crossings will be extended to 15 additional junctions in batches from the second half of this year under the Transport Strategy Blueprint.

zh.headline: 沙田石門站對角行人過路處啟用 步行距離料減三成
zh.dek: 運輸署周二啟用安明街與安睦街交界對角過路處，行人可一次過橫過路口，屬今年15個推展地點之一。
body: 運輸署周二公布，沙田安明街與安睦街交界路口的對角行人過路處已經啟用，行人可以較短距離一次過橫過至對角位置。
該過路處鄰近港鐵石門站及碩門商場。當局已增設下斜路邊石，便利長者、輪椅使用者和使用手推車人士，並加設交通護柱提醒駕駛人士小心駛過路口。
運輸署表示，2024年在沙田及尖沙咀兩個試驗路口整體運作安全暢順。預期對角過路的步行距離及時間較直角過路平均縮短約三成。根據《運輸策略藍圖》，對角行人過路處會推展至另外15個合適路口，並由今年下半年起分批啟用。
